title: Consolidate cloud-provider compatibility shims and optimize plan caching
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: Over the last 18 months we've accumulated multiple small provider compatibility shims across our Terraform modules to work around provider bugs and region-specific quirks (AWS, GCP, Azure). These shims reduce developer productivity (high plan churn, confusing diffs) and block provider upgrades. Separately, CI terraform plans are slow and noisy for routine changes because we lack a consistent plan-caching strategy and many modules re-evaluate provider-specific computed attributes on every run.

Goal: Consolidate compatibility shims into a small, well-documented provider-compat layer, introduce a plan-caching mechanism (cache keying by module fingerprint + variable hash), and add module-level guards to reduce spurious diffs. This should reduce CI plan noise by >=60%, speed up plan execution for infra CLs by ~30%, and unblock provider version bumping.

Scope:
- Audit existing shims across networking, vpc, eip, nat, and cni modules.
- Move common shims into a new modules/provider-compat/* surface with clear feature flags.
- Replace ad-hoc conditional logic in modules with stable callsites into provider-compat.
- Implement a lightweight plan cache in CI that stores 'terraform plan -out' artifacts keyed by module fingerprint + vars; invalidate when module code changes or provider version changes.
- Add explicit lifecycle ignore_changes and computed attribute normalization where safe to avoid noisy diffs.
- Document migration steps and provide a one-off plan rebase tool to capture changes for state refreshes.

Non-Goals: Full rewrite of modules; changing resource topology; introducing stateful orchestration outside Terraform.

Design decisions and rationale:
- Centralizing shims reduces duplication and concentrates risk when we remove temporary workarounds. Each shim will be feature-flagged with a deprecation timeline in comments.
- Plan cache will be implemented as an opt-in CI step (kept small, filesystem-backed in CI runners, and backed by an S3 artifact store for longer retention). We won’t attempt to cache apply outputs or state.
- Use module fingerprinting (git tree + module path + provider version) as cache key to reduce false invalidations.

Acceptance criteria:
- All existing provider shims either moved to modules/provider-compat or removed with a short justification.
- CI plan times for network-related changes reduced by >=30% in benchmark jobs.
- CI plan diff noise (measure: number of changed lines in plan output across identical variable change) reduced by >=60%.
- A migration doc is published with runbook for any necessary state refreshes and rollback steps.
- At least one provider major version bump (AWS provider) run in staging without manual shim reworks.

Rollout plan:
Phase 1 (Audit) - 1 week: Create inventory of shims (grep + module map). Capture owners and risk level.
Phase 2 (Compat Layer + Spec) - 2 weeks: Implement provider-compat module, move low-risk shims, add tests.
Phase 3 (Plan Cache + Guards) - 2 weeks: Build CI cache prototype, instrument perf metrics, add lifecycle ignore_changes where safe.
Phase 4 (Staged Migration) - 2 weeks: Migrate remaining shims behind feature flags and run smoke plans in staging.
Phase 5 (Cutover + Monitor) - 1 week: Remove flags, monitor plan noise, and run provider bump in staging.

Testing and validation:
- Unit test module behavior using kitchen-terraform or terratest where applicable.
- End-to-end CI plan benchmarks on representative workspaces (vpc, networking, ci-bootstrap).
- Manual validation: run terraform plan against staging workspaces and compare with baseline.
- Canary provider bump in a non-critical region.

Rollback and mitigation:
- All changes are non-destructive by default; any module migration includes a preserved legacy interface for one cycle.
- CI cache can be invalidated via a CI flag to return to baseline behavior.
- If provider bump causes regressions, revert to pinned provider version and escalate to provider support.

Risks:
- Mistagging computed attributes as stable could mask real configuration drift. Mitigation: conservative coverage and a manual rebase plan.
- Plan cache staleness causing missed deltas. Mitigation: strict invalidation rules and immediate ability to bypass cache.

Related artifacts:
- Audit spreadsheet: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/provider-compat-audit-2026
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/Provider+Compat+Layer+and+Plan+Cache
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/8421

Notes: This ticket focuses on infra-level developer experience and unlocks future provider upgrades and Terraform 1.6+ features. The work intersects with releases tracked in infra-2026.04 and depends on earlier state-safety work (ENG-582901).

2026-03-02 Marina Chen (review): Left review comments on naming and deprecation metadata. Agreed we should add explicit deprecation_date attribute in shim modules.
2026-03-06 Kevin Morales (security): Confirmed no secrets are introduced. Suggested adding a small IAM read-only test for provider behaviors when possible.

2026-03-10 Liam O'Connor: CI plan cache prototype ready in feature branch; benchmark job shows ~34% plan time reduction for vpc workspace when cache hits. Caveat: cache miss overhead ~6s for metadata checks.
